classes.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},{"text":"Ages differ by class.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson sorts out the kinds of licenses Arizona issues. First, a note about a number you give on every application. Your Social Security number is used to verify your identity and to comply with child support laws, and it is not used as your driver license number. Now the classes themselves. Arizona issues licenses by class: Class G for graduated, Class D for operator, Class M for motorcycle, and Classes A, B and C for commercial drivers. In the rest of the lesson we look at how a motorcycle privilege is added, what the operator and motorcycle licenses allow, the ages that go with them, and where commercial licenses are covered instead.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":45,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Operator and motorcycle licenses","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},"lines":[{"text":"Class D covers ordinary vehicles.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Class D needs age eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Class M from age sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here are the two licenses most new drivers ask about. A Class D operator license lets you drive any vehicle that does not require a motorcycle or commercial license, and you must be at least eighteen to apply for one. Riding a motorcycle or motor driven cycle requires a Class M license or endorsement, which you can apply for from age sixteen. Notice that the two ages are different, and that the motorcycle license is the one you can apply for first. That difference is one of the most useful numbers to remember from this lesson, so keep it in view as we go on.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Adding a motorcycle privilege","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F39"]},"lines":[{"text":"Combine Class M with another class.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F39"]},{"text":"Added as an endorsement.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F39"]},{"text":"Printed on the back.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F39"]}],"narration":{"text":"You do not always need a second card to ride. When a Class M license is combined with another class, the motorcycle privilege is added as an endorsement on the back of the current license. So a driver who already holds a Class D license and qualifies to ride gets the motorcycle privilege added to that same license rather than a separate one. Commercial drivers are handled differently again. A commercial driver license in Class A, B or C is required for commercial motor vehicles, and its requirements are covered in the separate CDL manual rather than this one. This manual focuses on the graduated, operator and motorcycle licenses.","fact_ids":["sec03-F03","sec03-F39"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Sixteen versus eighteen","fact_ids":["sec03-R12","sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},"lines":[{"text":"Class D: eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-R12","sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Class M: sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-R12","sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Do not swap them.","fact_ids":["sec03-R12","sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap in this lesson. Because eighteen is such a familiar age, people assume every license class waits until then. A Class D operator license needs age eighteen, while a Class M motorcycle license can be applied for at sixteen. So when a question asks about riding a motorcycle, think sixteen, and when it asks about a Class D operator license, think eighteen. Swapping the two ages is the classic slip on this topic. On any question about this, check whether it asks about riding a motorcycle or about the Class D license, and match the age to that license.","fact_ids":["sec03-R12","sec03-F36","sec03-F37"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":41,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Young motorcycle riders","fact_ids":["sec03-F38","sec03-F37"]},"lines":[{"text":"Six months on a motorcycle permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F38","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Approved course or certified riding.","fact_ids":["sec03-F38","sec03-F37"]},{"text":"Applies under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F38","sec03-F37"]}],"narration":{"text":"A rider under eighteen has extra steps before a Class M license. An under-eighteen motorcycle applicant needs at least six months holding an Arizona motorcycle permit, plus either an MVD-approved motorcycle course or a parent certifying thirty hours of supervised riding. The two options after the permit time are an approved course or a parent's certification of supervised riding. Either one completes the requirement, but the six months on an Arizona motorcycle permit comes first in both cases. That order stays the same for every rider under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F38","sec03-F37"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":35,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s6","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the class ages","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-R12"]},"lines":[{"text":"A Class D operator license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-R12"]},{"text":"What is the minimum age?","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-R12"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: at what age can you apply for a Class D operator license? Think before you hear the answer. The answer is eighteen. A Class D operator license lets you drive any vehicle that does not require a motorcycle or commercial license, and you must be at least eighteen to apply for one. If you said sixteen, you were thinking of the motorcycle license. A Class D operator license needs age eighteen, while a Class M motorcycle license can be applied for at sixteen. Keeping these two ages apart will help on several questions in this section.","fact_ids":["sec03-F36","sec03-R12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u01-s7","kind":"close","title":{"text":"License classes recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F36","sec03-F37","sec03-F38","sec03-F39","sec03-R12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Classes G, D, M, A, B and C.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F36","sec03-F37","sec03-F38","sec03-F39","sec03-R12"]},{"text":"Class D at eighteen; Class M at sixteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F36","sec03-F37","sec03-F38","sec03-F39","sec03-R12"]},{"text":"Commercial rules in the CDL manual.","fact_ids":["sec03-F01","sec03-F02","sec03-F03","sec03-F36","sec03-F37","sec03-F38","sec03-F39","sec03-R12"]}],"narration":{"text":"To close, your Social Security number verifies your identity and supports child support laws, and it is not your license number. Everything starts with one requirement. You must pass the Division written test before MVD will issue an Arizona instruction permit, though this rule does not cover Commercial Learner's Permits. In this lesson we cover the ages for each kind of permit, who must supervise you, how long each permit lasts, the special limits on motorcycle permits, and how to prepare for the written test that comes first. A graduated or motorcycle instruction permit is available once you are at least fifteen years and six months old, but an operator permit requires age eighteen. Permit ages split by permit type: fifteen years and six months for a graduated or motorcycle permit, but eighteen for an operator permit. So a teenager will usually start with a graduated permit, while an adult who is eighteen or older can go straight to an operator permit. The operator permit is the one that waits until eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-R01"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Who rides with you","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"lines":[{"text":"Licensed driver at least twenty-one.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Class A, B, C or D license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},{"text":"Sitting in the seat beside you.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]}],"narration":{"text":"A car permit never lets you drive alone. A graduated or operator permit holder must drive with a Class A, B, C or D licensed driver who is at least twenty-one and sits in the seat beside them. Each part of that rule is required. The supervisor must be old enough, must hold one of the listed license classes, and must sit right beside you rather than in the back seat. A licensed eighteen year old friend does not meet the rule, because the supervisor must be at least twenty-one. All three parts must be true at the same time for the practice drive to follow the rule.","fact_ids":["sec03-F05"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"How long permits last","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"Graduated and operator: twelve months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"Motorcycle: seven months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"One motorcycle renewal in twenty-four months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Permits do not last forever, and the lengths differ. Graduated and operator instruction permits are valid for twelve months. A motorcycle permit is valid for seven months and can be renewed only once within a twenty-four-month period. The manual puts the comparison in one sentence. Permit lengths differ by type: a graduated or operator permit lasts twelve months, while a motorcycle permit lasts seven months with one renewal allowed in twenty-four months. So check which permit you hold before counting the months, because the motorcycle permit runs out much sooner.","fact_ids":["sec03-F06","sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Motorcycle permit limits","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},"lines":[{"text":"No passengers.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},{"text":"No freeways or interstates.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},{"text":"No riding after dark or in poor light.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap for new riders. A motorcycle permit feels like freedom, but it comes with firm limits. A motorcycle permit holder may not carry passengers, may not ride on freeways or interstate highways, and may not ride between sunset and sunrise or whenever light is too poor to see people or vehicles five hundred feet away. Each limit is separate. You cannot carry a friend, you cannot use freeways or interstate highways, and you cannot ride from sunset to sunrise or in poor light. A ride that breaks any one of them is not allowed on a permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F07"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s6","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Preparing and transferring","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R09","sec03-F15"]},"lines":[{"text":"Practice the written test online.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R09","sec03-F15"]},{"text":"No written test rule for commercial permits.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R09","sec03-F15"]},{"text":"Out-of-state permit time counts.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R09","sec03-F15"]}],"narration":{"text":"MVD offers practice for the written test on its website, so you can prepare before your visit. The written test rule has one exclusion. The written test is required before an Arizona instruction permit, but the rule does not apply to a Commercial Learner's Permit. And if you held a permit somewhere else before moving here, that time is not lost. Arizona credits applicants for the time they held an instruction permit in another state. So a newcomer does not have to restart the permit clock from zero. Both points help you start the permit stage prepared.","fact_ids":["sec03-F09","sec03-R09","sec03-F15"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check permit lengths","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},"lines":[{"text":"A motorcycle instruction permit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},{"text":"How long is it valid?","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a quick check: how long is a motorcycle instruction permit valid, and how often can it be renewed? The answer is seven months, renewable only once within a twenty-four-month period. A motorcycle permit is valid for seven months and can be renewed only once within a twenty-four-month period. If you said twelve months, you were thinking of the graduated and operator permits. Permit lengths differ by type: a graduated or operator permit lasts twelve months, while a motorcycle permit lasts seven months with one renewal allowed in twenty-four months. The motorcycle permit is the shorter one.","fact_ids":["sec03-F08","sec03-R02"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u02-s8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Permit rules recap","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-R01","sec03-R02","sec03-R09"]},"lines":[{"text":"Written test first.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-R01","sec03-R02","sec03-R09"]},{"text":"Ages, supervisor and lengths.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-R01","sec03-R02","sec03-R09"]},{"text":"Motorcycle limits.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-R01","sec03-R02","sec03-R09"]}],"narration":{"text":"To finish, you must pass the Division written test before MVD issues an instruction permit, except for a Commercial Learner's Permit. Graduated and motorcycle permits start at fifteen years and six months, and an operator permit at eighteen. A car permit holder drives with a licensed driver at least twenty-one sitting alongside. Graduated and operator permits last twelve months, and a motorcycle permit lasts seven months with one renewal. Motorcycle permit holders carry no passengers, avoid freeways and do not ride after dark, and permit time from another state is credited.","fact_ids":["sec03-F04","sec03-F05","sec03-F06","sec03-F07","sec03-F08","sec03-F14","sec03-F15","sec03-R01","sec03-R02","sec03-R09"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec03-u03","module_id":"sec03-m03","objective_ids":["sec03-u03"],"title":{"text":"Graduated license limits","fact_ids":["sec03-F10","sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},"why_how":[{"text":"The first six months of a graduated license come with night and passenger limits, and breaking them carries extra penalties.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F13"]}],"worked_example":{"scenario":{"text":"Liam, sixteen, got his graduated license two months ago and wants to drive home from a party at one in the morning.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},"reasoning":{"text":"That drive falls between midnight and five in the morning during his first six months, and a party is not one of the exempt trips.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-F12","sec03-R04"]},"result":{"text":"Liam cannot make that drive alone unless a licensed parent or legal guardian rides in the front passenger seat.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R03"]}},"misconception":{"claim":{"text":"Common mistake: thinking siblings count against the graduated passenger limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05"]},"correction":{"text":"Siblings never count; it is non-sibling passengers under eighteen that are limited to one without a licensed parent or guardian up front.","fact_ids":["sec03-R05","sec03-F13"]}},"memory_support":{"text":"Midnight to five, one young friend, siblings free.","fact_ids":["sec03-R04","sec03-R05"]},"self_check":{"prompt":{"text":"During the first six months, a graduated driver drives home from a job at one in the morning. Is that allowed?","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]},"answer":{"text":"Yes, driving directly to or from a job is exempt from the night limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12"]},"rationale":{"text":"The night limit does not apply to trips directly to or from a job, a school activity, a religious activity or a family emergency.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Your first graduated months","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Who gets a graduated license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},{"text":"A night limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},{"text":"A passenger limit.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]}],"narration":{"text":"This lesson covers the graduated license and the limits that come with it at the start. Here is who it is for. A graduated license goes to applicants who are at least sixteen but under eighteen and lets them drive any vehicle that needs no motorcycle or commercial license. For the first six months, two limits apply: one about the hours you may drive and one about who may ride with you. We will look at each limit, the exceptions to it, and the details that are easiest to get wrong. Both limits end once the first six months are over.","fact_ids":["sec03-F10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The night limit","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},"lines":[{"text":"Off the road from midnight to five.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"During the first six months.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},{"text":"A licensed parent up front lifts it.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the first limit. During the first six months, a graduated license holder must stay off the road from midnight to five a.m., except when the front passenger seat is occupied by a parent or legal guardian holding a valid Class A, B, C or D license. The manual repeats the time window in a short form. The graduated night limit runs from midnight to five a.m. and lasts only for the first six months of the license. So the limit has a start, an end and an expiration. It covers midnight to five in the morning, and only during the first six months of the graduated license.","fact_ids":["sec03-F11","sec03-R04"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Trips that are exempt","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Sanctioned school activities.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]},{"text":"Work.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]},{"text":"Religious activities and family emergencies.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Some trips are allowed even inside the night window. The night limit also does not apply when the teen is driving directly to or from a sanctioned school-sponsored activity, a job, a sanctioned religious activity or a family emergency. The word directly matters here. The exception covers going straight to or from one of those places, not stopping somewhere else along the way. These trips are the only exceptions besides a licensed parent or legal guardian riding in front. A detour to a friend's house or a restaurant would not be a direct trip.","fact_ids":["sec03-F12","sec03-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Supervisor or parent?","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F05","sec03-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Permit supervisor: any qualifying adult.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F05","sec03-F11"]},{"text":"Night limit: parent or guardian.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F05","sec03-F11"]},{"text":"Different adults, different rules.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F05","sec03-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is a trap that catches many families. An adult who could supervise a permit holder cannot always lift the night limit. The permit supervisor must be at least twenty-one and hold a Class A, B, C or D license, while the adult who lifts the graduated night limit must be the teen's parent or legal guardian. So a licensed aunt who is thirty could ride with a permit holder, but she does not lift the graduated night limit. Only a parent or legal guardian with a valid Class A, B, C or D license does that. The difference is who the adult is, not only how old they are.","fact_ids":["sec03-R03","sec03-F05","sec03-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec03-u03-s5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The passenger limit","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-R05"]},"lines":[{"text":"At most one passenger under eighteen.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"Siblings do not count.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-R05"]},{"text":"Unless a licensed parent rides up front.","fact_ids":["sec03-F13","sec03-R05"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the second limit. During the first six months, a graduated license holder may not drive with more than one passenger under age eighteen, unless those passengers are the teen's siblings or a licensed parent or legal guardian rides in the front passenger seat.
